description: FINDING 2 plus FINDING 3 plus the single dated doc. Finding 2: session/auth responses carry no Cache-Control while a GET body can contain the CSRF token, and these travel through the Amplify /api/<*> status-200 rewrite, so a shared cache could serve one customer's CSRF token to another. lambda_utils/response.py::cors_headers sets no Cache-Control and is NOT an owned path (and core/contacts/handler.py:285 deliberately removed it, so a blanket change there would be wrong). customer_session.py has no response builder at all and no handler imports it yet. Fix: add the no-store header contract to customer_session.py and apply it at the two auth handlers we own; report the already-deployed wecare-customer-session handler, whose source is not in this tree. Finding 3: measured and confirmed live - inline policy wecare-digital-lambda-permissions on wecare-digital-lambda-role, Sid DynamoDB, grants UpdateItem and DeleteItem with NO condition on table/stack-wecare-digital-*, which matches the now-ACTIVE stack-wecare-digital-CustomerSessionsTable; 62 of 68 functions are on that role and ZERO of them reference the table. Narrowing is provably unused but is still a production IAM change on a shared role, so it is an owner-approval report item. Read .agents/tasks/phone-normalisation-fix-20261001/plan.md sections 0.5, 0.6, 1.6, 1.7 and 4 before starting. Depends on FEAT-001 only for the doc's Finding 1 content - read FEAT-001.json's findings field.
steps: Read plan.md sections 0.5, 0.6, 1.6, 1.7 and 4, and read amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/customer_session.py end to end before editing it.

Add NO_STORE_HEADERS = {'Cache-Control': 'no-store', 'Pragma': 'no-cache'} and def harden_session_headers(headers: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> Dict[str, str] to customer_session.py, in its existing 'cookie assembly' section beside build_set_cookie, and export both from __all__. Pragma is included because that is the pair the repo already uses at edge/get-miss-redirect/handler.py:83; ai/mcp/handler.py:568 and core/site-language/handler.py:198 use no-store alone, so this matches the stricter existing pattern.

Document in the docstring why this is necessary rather than defensive: the response body carries SessionView.csrf_token, the responses travel through the Amplify /api/<*> status-200 rewrite, and a shared cache serving one customer's CSRF token to another defeats the double-submit check that build_set_cookie's SameSite=Lax choice explicitly relies on.

Apply the no-store pair to EVERY return path of amplify/functions/auth/customer-registration/handler.py - _request, _verify, the handler-level error return, the 502 send_failed return, and options_response - using a small local wrapper that merges NO_STORE_HEADERS into the cors_response result. Do NOT modify lambda_utils/response.py.
Apply the same treatment to every return path of amplify/functions/auth/email-verification/handler.py.

Write tests/test_session_response_is_not_cacheable.py: harden_session_headers produces both headers and preserves any headers handed to it; every customer-registration and email-verification return path carries Cache-Control: no-store; and a guard asserting a response body carrying a csrfToken key cannot be built without the header.

Confirm the cross-workstream precondition holds and record it: this change adds RESPONSE headers only. It does not enable assert_csrf on any route and adds no required request header, so src/pages/cart.tsx (~line 149) and src/pages/checkout/status.tsx (~line 159), which gate on getSession() and send no CSRF header, cannot break. If you find yourself about to call assert_csrf anywhere, that is out of scope - STOP and call send_message with severity warning.
Run the three AWS READ commands in plan.md section 4 verbatim and capture their output. These are reads; attempt no iam put-role-policy, no iam create-policy, no iam delete-role-policy.

Write docs/execution/phone-normalisation-fix-20261001.md - the ONE dated doc permitted by this task. Cover: Finding 1's reproduction table before and after, the two implementations and why they are duplicated (standalone packaging), the four entry points wired and the ones deliberately not with reasons, and the plan.md 1.5 contract change at the registration door; Finding 2's three fix sites plus the wecare-customer-session report item naming harden_session_headers as the exact call to add; Finding 3 as an owner-approval item carrying the plan.md 0.6 evidence table, the section 4 command output, and the proposed explicit-Deny statement verbatim.

Use the maintenance-reporting status vocabulary in the doc. Mark Finding 3 as NEEDS CONFIRMATION with severity HIGH, and give impact, current state, desired state, rollback (delete the added inline policy) and the simulate-principal-policy command to verify after approval. Record that the recommended option is a NEW inline policy containing an explicit Deny on the session table ARN for the four mutating actions, rejecting the alternative of narrowing the existing stack-wecare-digital-* wildcard because that changes the grant for all 62 functions to fix one table. DO NOT APPLY IT.
Put no credential value, no full phone number and no raw Secrets Manager value in the doc. Secret and table names, ARNs, role names, policy names, commit ids and command text are all fine.

FILES CHANGED (5):
  1. amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/customer_session.py   +39, additive only. NO_STORE_HEADERS = {'Cache-Control': 'no-store', 'Pragma': 'no-cache'} and harden_session_headers(headers: Optional[Dict[str,str]] = None) -> Dict[str,str], placed in the existing 'cookie assembly' section immediately before read_cookie (i.e. beside build_set_cookie / build_clear_cookie), both appended to __all__. Returns a NEW dict and never mutates its input; the no-store pair WINS over any weaker Cache-Control the caller passed, which is pinned by a test - a session response with max-age is a bug, not a preference. Docstring carries the CDN reasoning (Amplify /api/<*> status-200 rewrite), the csrf_token-in-the-body reasoning, the SameSite=Lax dependency, and the explicit reason response.py was NOT changed.
  2. amplify/functions/auth/customer-registration/handler.py     local def _no_store(response) wrapper added under `logger = get_logger(__name__)`; import line became `from lambda_utils import customer_session, otp_throttle`. Applied at 5 return sites: _reply (covers both _request's success and _verify's success), the OPTIONS preflight, the handler-level 500, the 502 send_failed, and the 400 CODE_REQUIRED.
  3. amplify/functions/auth/email-verification/handler.py        same wrapper; import became `from lambda_utils import customer_session, otp_challenge, otp_throttle`. Applied at ALL 12 return sites, including `otp_throttle.throttled_response(...)` - which does NOT go through cors_response and would otherwise have been the one uncovered path. A cached 429 would misreport another caller's remaining budget, so it needed the header as much as a 200 did.
  4. tests/test_session_response_is_not_cacheable.py             NEW, 21 tests.
  5. docs/execution/phone-normalisation-fix-20261001.md           NEW, 394 lines, the ONE permitted doc. Nothing created under docs/execution/snapshots/.

TEST DESIGN, and one deliberate strengthening beyond the plan: the plan asked for 'every return path carries Cache-Control: no-store'. A purely behavioural test can only reach the paths it can provoke without AWS, and the finding is about EVERY path, so the file does both:
  - a per-file AST guard (test_every_returned_response_is_hardened) that finds every `return <call>` whose callee is cors_response / options_response / error_response / throttled_response and fails unless it is wrapped in _no_store. Mirrors tests/test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py, and for the same reason: both handlers' docstrings legitimately name cors_response, so grep would false-positive.
  - test_the_guard_actually_found_something, asserting >= 5 matched returns per file, because a walker that silently matches nothing proves nothing.
  - test_the_wrapper_goes_through_the_shared_contract, asserting neither handler hard-codes the literal 'Cache-Control' - the pair is defined once in customer_session.
  - test_response_py_is_not_the_place_this_was_fixed, asserting response.py contains no Cache-Control at all. This pins the NEGATIVE decision so a future session cannot 'tidy it up' into the shared builder and silently override core/contacts/handler.py:285.
  - behavioural proof on the paths reachable with zero AWS: OPTIONS preflight on both handlers, registration verify-without-code 400, email INVALID_EMAIL 400, and a monkeypatched 500 on both. Each asserts Cache-Control no-store AND Pragma no-cache AND that Content-Type / Access-Control-Allow-Origin survived the merge.
  - the csrfToken tripwire: scans every amplify/functions/**/handler.py and fails if a `csrfToken` string CONSTANT appears (AST constants, docstrings excluded) in a module that does not call harden_session_headers. Vacuous today (no handler returns one yet - tests/test_checkout_package_completeness.py:42 records customer_session 'ships ahead'), so it carries a positive control proving the detector fires on `{"csrfToken": ...}` and does NOT fire on prose mentioning it.

This is the load-bearing read for the recommendation: the legitimate custodian is granted by its OWN inline policy, so denying the shared role costs the session function nothing.

Full Sid list in that policy: CloudWatchLogs, DynamoDB, S3Access, WhatsApp, PinpointSMSVoice, SES, SQS, SNS, Bedrock, SecretsManager, CloudWatchMetrics, Polly, HealthAndAdvisor.
  NO IAM WRITE ATTEMPTED: no put-role-policy, no create-policy, no delete-role-policy, no attach/detach. The shared role was neither narrowed nor widened. The doc's proposed change is a NEW inline policy with an explicit Deny on the session table ARN for PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/BatchWriteItem, marked NEEDS CONFIRMATION / severity HIGH, with impact, current state, desired state, zero measured blast radius, the rejected wildcard-narrowing alternative, the one-call rollback (delete-role-policy wecare-digital-session-table-deny) and the post-approval simulate command.
